summary: Mapped the selected WebRTC microphone ID to Android AudioRecord's AudioDeviceInfo ID so the local-only microphone check works for built-in microphones on Pixel.

checks.name: Audio-device mapping tests
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/audio_device_check_test.dart test/android_audio_devices_test.dart
checks.observation: All 10 targeted tests passed, including Android ID mapping, name fallback, and ensuring the native mapping method is not called on desktop.

checks.name: Release APK and Pixel 7 runtime test
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi --no-pub; adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-v8a-release.apk
checks.observation: Signed arm64 release APK installed in place on Pixel 7 (Android 17/API 37), preserving app data. Local microphone test entered its active state without the previous device-not-found error. The user spoke next to the phone and confirmed that it worked. A later accessibility snapshot, taken after speech ended, showed 0% as the meter had returned to silence. The test was stopped immediately afterward; no voice channel was joined and no audio was sent to LiveKit.

remaining: Test external microphone hotplug and selected-input switching on Android; verify local test and input switching on macOS and Windows.
